summary: Multiple vessels were struck in the Strait of Hormuz, including the Indian bulk carrier Cape Dao attacked by Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps, killing one and wounding another, while a separate explosion was reported in Bandar Abbas. China has conducted over 1,300 dual-use military shipments to Iran and thousands of components to Houthi forces, significantly bolstering regional missile and drone capabilities. The IDF activated Division 98 headquarters in Judea and Samaria to bolster command and control amid recent security incidents.
key_points: The Indian bulk carrier Cape Dao was struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, resulting in one death and one injury, with the ship evacuated and burning; the attack was attributed to Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps (Source: @VahidOnline/78499).

China conducted over 1,300 dual-use military shipments to Iran in the past year for its missile and drone industries, with approximately 35% of all military items intercepted en route to the Houthis between 2021 and 2025 originating from China (Source: @asafroz/53728).

The IDF activated Division 98 headquarters in Judea and Samaria to assume command over the Judea and Azion brigades, citing recent events and the need to strengthen defense and attack capabilities in the region (Source: @New_security8200/203911).

A severe explosion was reported in Bandar Abbas at 00:13, with strong shockwaves felt and windows shaking, described as a sea explosion; a separate explosion at the Strait of Hormuz was recorded at 22:13 Tehran time (Source: @VahidOnline/78505).
Yemeni armed forces reportedly drove out Saudi mercenaries and imposed full control over the Taiz-Aden front line (Source: @naya_foriraq/91419).
Kurdish opposition bases in Erbil, northern Iraq, were struck and set ablaze by drone attacks (Source: @naya_foriraq/91423).

Neria Litrat, son of Israel's ambassador to the US, was severely wounded in a ramming attack at a checkpoint and underwent complex brain surgery; his condition remains very serious and life-threatening (Source: @almogboker78/18249).

sections.executive_summary: The Strait of Hormuz has become an active theater of hostilities, with the Indian bulk carrier Cape Dao struck by Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps and a separate explosion reported in Bandar Abbas, severely disrupting regional maritime commerce. China's sustained military supply chain to Iran and Houthi forces, exceeding 1,300 dual-use shipments in the past year, is fundamentally altering the balance of power in the region. Concurrently, the IDF has activated Division 98 in the West Bank as tensions mount across multiple fronts.
iran: China conducted over 1,300 shipments of dual-use items to Iran in the past year, specifically supporting Iran's missile and drone industries. Approximately 35% of all military items intercepted en route to the Houthis between 2021 and 2025 originated from China, compared to only 5% between 2015 and 2018, indicating a dramatic escalation in Chinese military support (Source: @asafroz/53728).

Chinese companies have become the primary source of goods intercepted heading to Houthi forces, including drone components, satellite communication devices manufactured in Chengdu, and screens from Guangdong province usable with unmanned vessels. Houthi-linked traders have learned Mandarin to operate in Chinese markets (Source: @asafroz/53723).

A strong explosion was reported in Bandar Abbas at 00:13 Tehran time, with shockwaves felt across the city and windows shaking; the incident was described as a sea explosion. A separate explosion at the Strait of Hormuz was recorded at 22:13 Tehran time (Source: @VahidOnline/78505).

The Indian bulk carrier Cape Dao was struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, resulting in one fatality and one injury. The ship was evacuated and is burning. The attack was attributed to the Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps (Source: @VahidOnline/78499).

Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi told his German counterpart that Germany's support enables Israel's continued occupation and war in West Asia, calling for an end to complicity and for Israel to be held accountable (Source: @presstv/208041).

US Secretary of State Rubio stated that the meeting with Iranian officials was positive but did not achieve a breakthrough. Iranian official Mohsen Rezaei stated the US has 4 to 5 days to comply with Iran's conditions (Source: @naya_foriraq/91384, @rodast_omiddana/81352).

Iranian President Pezeshkian addressed the 81st UNGA, combining messages of defiance against US pressure with readiness for diplomacy. Foreign media described his speech as a mix of strong criticism of Trump's approach and emphasis on negotiation without language of force, with the Strait of Hormuz emerging as a key axis of the dispute (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/394438).
israel: The IDF activated Division 98 headquarters in Judea and Samaria to assume command over the Judeh and Azion brigades, citing recent events and the need to strengthen defense and attack capabilities during this tense period. The activation was ordered by Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir (Source: @New_security8200/203911).

Neria Litrat, son of Israel's ambassador to the US Yehiel Litrat, was severely wounded in a ramming attack at a checkpoint. He underwent complex brain surgery lasting several hours alongside additional treatments; his condition remains very serious with life-threatening risks (Source: @almogboker78/18249, @almogboker78/18254).
Prime Minister Netanyahu visited Shari Zedek Hospital where Neria Litrat is hospitalized before departing for the UN General Assembly in New York (Source: @amitsegal/65139).
The Knesset unanimously removed the defamation that former PM Aaron Barak had leveled against terror-supporting MKs, clearing the record (Source: @amitsegal/65124).

US officials drafted a statement condemning the UK, France, and Canada over plans to block imports from Israeli settlements in the West Bank, but the statement was never released due to lack of consultation with White House and State Department leadership (Source: @Faytuks_Network/7430).

The Israeli Navy is set to receive its sixth submarine, INS Drakon, a Dolphin 2-class vessel measuring 74 meters and weighing 2,600 tons, arriving from Germany after a 3,792-nautical-mile voyage. The Navy plans to massively expand its fleet to contend with maritime threats in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb (Source: @manniefabian/59224).

RM Mansour Abbas mocked Netanyahu in response to the Central Elections Committee's decision to disqualify his party, claiming Netanyahu chose not to cooperate with disqualification efforts in previous elections while personally negotiating with him in Balfour (Source: @yediotnews25/135277).
gaza_west_bank: Yehiel Litrat, Israel's ambassador to the US, lost his son who was killed by Hamas in Gaza. His other son Neria was severely wounded in a ramming attack at a checkpoint in the West Bank (Source: @yediotnews25/135288, @almogboker78/18249).
A Palestinian militant attempted to stab IDF soldiers at a checkpoint, according to US Ambassador Hackman's statement (Source: @yediotnews25/135288).
An incident was reported at Maccabim checkpoint with a wounded individual, though details remain sparse (Source: @pkpoi/144043).

The IDF activated Division 98 headquarters in Judea and Samaria to bolster command and control over the Judea and Azion brigades, citing recent events and the need to enhance security during this tense period (Source: @New_security8200/203911).
lebanon: Spanish PM Sánchez addressed the 81st UNGA, stating Spain has opposed every war of aggression over the past eight years including in Lebanon, imposed an arms embargo on Israel, and banned the use of its territory for illegal aggression against Iran (Source: @presstv/208042).
syria_iraq: Kurdish opposition bases in Erbil, northern Iraq, were struck by drone attacks and set ablaze (Source: @naya_foriraq/91423).

Analysts report that behind the protests in Syria, Israeli forces are operating to clear and consolidate power, with regions including Quneitra, Daraa, and Damascus suburbs expected to come under Israeli control (Source: @kianmeli1/92399).
gulf_states: Yemeni armed forces reportedly drove out Saudi mercenaries and imposed full control over the Taiz-Aden front line (Source: @naya_foriraq/91419).

The Strait of Hormuz has become a critical flashpoint, with attacks on commercial shipping and explosions in Bandar Abbas threatening Gulf maritime security and global shipping routes (Source: @VahidOnline/78499, @VahidOnline/78505).
key_developments: The Indian bulk carrier Cape Dao was struck by Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps in the Strait of Hormuz, killing one and wounding another, with the vessel burning and evacuated; a separate explosion was reported in Bandar Abbas, signaling escalating maritime hostilities in one of the world's most critical waterways (Source: @VahidOnline/78499).

China conducted over 1,300 dual-use military shipments to Iran in the past year for missile and drone production, with approximately 35% of all military items intercepted en route to Houthis between 2021-2025 originating from China, fundamentally reshaping regional military capabilities (Source: @asafroz/53728).

The IDF activated Division 98 headquarters in Judea and Samaria under Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir to assume command over the Judea and Azion brigades, citing recent security events and the need to strengthen defense and attack capabilities in the West Bank (Source: @New_security8200/203911).

Neria Litrat, son of Israel's ambassador to the US, was severely wounded in a ramming attack at a West Bank checkpoint and underwent complex brain surgery; his condition remains life-threatening, compounding the Litrat family's grief after his brother was killed by Hamas in Gaza (Source: @almogboker78/18249).

Kurdish opposition bases in Erbil, northern Iraq, were struck and burned by drone attacks, indicating expanding aerial operations targeting non-state armed groups in the region (Source: @naya_foriraq/91423).

Yemeni armed forces reportedly drove out Saudi-backed mercenaries and imposed full control over the Taiz-Aden front line, further consolidating Houthi territorial gains in Yemen (Source: @naya_foriraq/91419).

Iranian President Pezeshkian addressed the 81st UNGA combining defiance against US pressure with readiness for diplomacy, while the Strait of Hormuz emerged as a central axis of the Tehran-Washington dispute over navigation rights and sanctions (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/394438).
sections.threat_assessment: The Strait of Hormuz has transitioned from a diplomatic flashpoint to an active combat zone, with confirmed attacks on commercial shipping and explosions near Iranian port infrastructure, posing severe risks to global energy transit. China's sustained military supply chain to Iran and Houthi forces, exceeding 1,300 dual-use shipments annually, is systematically enhancing adversary missile and drone production capacity beyond what sanctions can interdict. The IDF's activation of Division 98 in the West Bank signals anticipation of expanded operational requirements across multiple fronts simultaneously. Iran's stated readiness for diplomacy alongside its continued maritime aggression suggests a dual-track strategy of escalation and negotiation. The convergence of these developments indicates a high probability of further kinetic incidents in the coming days.
sections.regional_response: European actors are increasingly vocal against Israeli military operations, with Spain imposing arms embargoes and banning territory use for aggression against Iran, while the US internally drafted but withheld a statement condemning allies' settlement-related trade restrictions. Iran's diplomatic posture at the UNGA balanced defiance with openness to negotiation, rejecting US demands while leaving the door open for dialogue. Saudi Arabia faces mounting pressure as Yemeni forces consolidate control over the Taiz-Aden line, undermining Riyadh's regional proxy objectives. Germany's role as a submarine supplier to Israel highlights continued Western military support despite political friction over Gaza operations.
sections.intelligence_notes: The Litrat family incident — ambassador Yehiel Litrat's son killed in Gaza and another son Neria severely wounded in the West Bank — carries significant diplomatic and psychological implications for US-Israel relations. China's deepening military-logistical ties with both Iran and Houthis, including traders learning Mandarin and establishing supply networks in Chinese cities, represent a structural shift that existing sanctions regimes have failed to reverse. The Bandar Abbas explosion and Strait of Hormuz attacks occurring within hours of each other suggest coordinated or cascading maritime operations. Israeli intelligence should monitor for potential retaliatory strikes on Chinese-linked entities and assess whether the Erbil drone strikes signal an expanded Iraqi theater of operations.
